correctness.rationale: Uniform gamma-beta ratio gives mean 1/2, variance 1/12 per pair. Direct exponential-integral quadrature produces the projection q and ζ in (0,1/24); distinct shared-index edge pairs have covariance exactly ζ. Counting all pair intersections yields the finite sample variance. With B fixed the tagged-edge graph has bounded dependency degree, overlapping common edges of independent matchings are O_p(1), and higher cumulants vanish after Gaussian scaling; B→∞ uses U-statistic CLT and an L² matching-remainder bound. Boundary N=2 checked explicitly, rate λ cancels. The included standalone checker completed 54 assertions, including independently randomized matching simulations. Numerical checks corroborate but do not prove asymptotic limits.

originality.rationale: The full publicly accessible 2023 article defines the paired-ratio statistic and B=50 random re-pairings, and its Theorem 1 is for the individual fixed-threshold statistic. The assessed novelty is an exact finite-N variance and CLT for repeated re-pairings of the SAME dataset at the natural zero-threshold baseline, including a kernel-specific projection constant and sharp B=50 variance ratios. The earlier open 2021 thesis covers the underlying test and simulations but its materially inspected Chapter 2 portions do not give the claimed formula. General incomplete U-statistic and Rao-Blackwell tools are credited rather than presented as new. Both private prior claims and current semantic research records were searched. Priority uncertainty remains for inaccessible book chapter and synonymous statistics.
residual_risks: The 2022 CRC Press precursor chapter was not available in full, and might contain stronger pairing analysis.
The older thesis was materially inspected in relevant sections, not comprehensively compared line-by-line in Greek.

The zero-threshold result does not cover the positive/adaptive thresholds important for the published tail test.

value.rationale: The original implementation recommends 50 random re-pairings specifically to control random pairing variability, yet the same dataset is reused and the repeats are dependent. The exact all-N variance quantifies the irreducible floor, establishes that 50 pairings capture exactly 98% of the removable matching variation, and identifies a non-obvious ~0.3932 one-pairing variance fraction and hypothetical ~19.66-fold independence calibration error. This is a natural zero-threshold baseline explicitly plotted in the source, a meaningful quantitative design and calibration law rather than arbitrary slice. Does not assert positive-threshold effects or that original calibrations are wrong.
